Phase 2: Merge with every name kept

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a projected slide with a referent nobody can resolve. Closest: L70 'the stance you kept' (chunk 4) and L72 'the tree file'. 'the stance' is named in chunk 3 bullets L58-60 (assumption tester / reframer / planner); 'the tree file' is a session artifact of the Phase 2 merge, exempt under the session-artifacts carve-out. L15 'The outcome from ./crux.md' is named by path. L37 'your memory' is the memory/ the student gathered in the prior exercise (arc-earned).

Harm: a callback whose target depends on deck position. L7 'Pick the outcome', L76 'Choose the bet' name the exercises by title (module-order siblings apt101-pick-the-outcome.md and apt101-choose-the-bet.md exist); no 'the earlier lecture'-style positional pointer. grep 'opening|earlier|previous' in body → none.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a pointer to a beat that no longer exists. Candidates: L7 'the outcome you agreed in Pick the outcome' (exercises/apt101-pick-the-outcome.md exists), L37 'back in your first session' (the gather-the-evidence session that produced memory/, same arc), L76 'You choose from it in Choose the bet' (apt101-choose-the-bet.md exists). Verified by ls.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a demo beat with no scene under a muted read. No guess-before-reveal beat in this file (no 'guess', 'predict'). Closest: L39 'Three subagents fanning out at once.' is a verbless fragment but it narrates a run the student starts one line earlier, not a demo reveal, and is followed by a verbed steer ('If one starts reading the world, stop it'). See suggestion.

Harm: a slide saying nothing standalone. Smallest chunk is chunk 1 (L11-19): three paragraphs, each with its own claim (sketch alone, what to write, put down the opportunity only you would think of). Every chunk carries a task.

Harm: header contradicted by its slide. Closest: chunk 3 'Read the evidence three ways' (L33) vs content L37-60: three stance subagents, three role reads, i.e. three ways. True. Chunk 2 'Merge with every name kept' vs L25-31: merge keeping names. True.

Harm: a cadence tic becoming the whole slide. grep for 'Not X. Not Y.' → none; no anaphora triple (closest L25 'the designer... the product owner... the team lead' are three distinct roles with distinct verbs); no superlatives; no number+retraction; no abstraction stack (closest L7 'customer needs, pains and wishes' is a concrete list); L17 'asked for, worked around' legs each concrete. L19 'The ones all three of you saw will turn up anyway.' is one declarative.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: maintainer dialect on a projected wall. grep -iE 'beat|compendium|forcing function|firing|mood|writing surface' over body L1-77 → 0 hits ('beat' appears only in the maintainer block after L78). 'stance' / 'subagents' are the reused A101 prompt's ordinary words.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold sprayed so nothing is a handle. Body bold elements: L5 'What you do:' (field label), L58-60 three role:stance leads. L58 '**Product owner: the assumption tester.**' is a coined stance handle (5 words), not a whole sentence; the three are the named stances of the reused prompt and read as checklist item names. Chunk 3 is over the 'most slides' ≤1 line but each bold names one of three parallel handles, which the rule allows for sets of named terms. Judgement PASS; see notes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/apt101-grow-the-tree.md --report -> slides: 4, oversized: 0; largest Phase 3 at 163 words / 3 bullets (limits 210/6).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a declarative heading mislabelled or a label heading where the slide owes a claim. Exercise headings are phase labels: 'Phase 1: Sketch alone', 'Phase 2: Merge with every name kept', 'Phase 3: Read the evidence three ways', 'Phase 4: Question the tree from your role' (L11, 21, 33, 66). Matches the exercise grammar; no law slide that owes a claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a bullet restating what the slide holds. Closest: L76 'The tree is not finished, and it should not be.' could read as a closing kicker, but it does not restate the header (Question the tree from your role) and sets the expectation that the next exercise chooses from it; L19 'Put down the opportunity only you would think of.' is a move. No doctrine restatement or design commentary found.
